# FreeType outline fixtures

`quadratic.ttf` and `cubic.otf` are original fonts containing one closed curved glyph at U+0043. Both use 1024 units per em, ascent 896, descent -128, zero line gap, and advance 1024. They contain no hint instructions or third-party outlines. The quadratic path runs from (128, 128) through control point (512, 896) to (896, 128), then returns along the horizontal chord. Degree elevation gives cubic control points (384, 640) and (640, 640), so both fonts describe the same parabola.

`expected.json` records font hashes, original control points, and pixel coverage at 16, 17, and 32 pixels per em. Coverage comes from analytic integration of the parabola, not renderer output. At scale `s = size / 1024`, the upper boundary is `512s - (x - 512s)^2 / (384s)` and the lower boundary is `128s`, between `128s` and `896s`. Each pixel is split at its intersections with the upper boundary; the polynomial integral gives the clipped area. Total coverage equals `196608s²`. The floating-point `alpha` grid stores area multiplied by 255 over the complete line height and advance.

FreeType rounds the descender down to a pixel boundary, giving baseline distances 2, 3, and 4 at these sizes. The glyph origin is at `line_height - baseline`, so the 17 pixel reference accounts for its integer text baseline. TrueType and CFF glyph bounding boxes can differ without changing this geometry.

ThorVG approximates curves with chords. Its fixed rasterizer stops subdivision when each control point's perpendicular distance to the chord is at most approximately 1/6 pixel. The curve's distance is at most 3/4 of that value. For these contours, the termination check rejects depths below three: sizes 16 and 17 use depth three throughout, and size 32 uses depths three and four. All subdivision midpoints lie exactly on the 1/256 pixel grid. A depth `d` chord has a maximum vertical error of `3 × size / (8 × 4^d)`, so `curve_deviation_pixels = 3 × size / 512` bounds every segment without reproducing renderer pixels.

`coverage_min` and `coverage_max` also account for RLE intersection rounding. Segment coordinate differences are at most 1344 subpixels and slopes at most two; the reciprocal intersection calculation introduces less than `2 × (1 + 1344 / 65536) / 256 < 1/64` pixel of vertical error. The lower envelope moves the parabola down by `curve_deviation_pixels + 1/64`; the upper envelope moves it up by `1/64`. Both keep the original horizontal range and bottom chord. Analytic integration gives their pixel areas. RLE coverage uses a factor of 256 and signed rounding, so the stored coverage bounds are `floor(256 × lower_area)` and `ceil(256 × upper_area)`, clamped to `[0, 255]`.

Tests composite these coverage bounds with text opacity against an opaque background. The vector backend mixes color alpha and text opacity with an eight-bit right shift; the reference uses `floor(255 × opacity / 256)` before source-over. Pixels outside the upper envelope are exact background. Colors inside the envelope allow two levels for integer premultiplication/compositing. This geometry bound is specific to these fonts and sizes. The existing polygon fonts and expected pixels in `../freetype/` retain their stricter coverage checks and cover metrics, kerning, composite glyphs, fallback, and cache lifetimes.
